bugs.summary: Warn in library(include.only=) calls where that directive is ignored
bugs.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text:
Following up r-devel thread https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2024-April/083319.html.

This is Martin's suggestion:

```
    >> I would assume that

    >> library(Matrix, include.only="isDiagonal")

    >> implies that only `isDiagonal` ends up on the search path

    > This could also be a reasonable behavior, but neither does that happen
    > today.

Indeed; I think we should signal a warning at least in the case
it does not happen --- namely when "parts of Matrix" are already
in the search path.
```

I have interpreted this conservatively so that

```
library(Matrix)
library(Matrix)
```

Gives no warning, neither does

```
library(Matrix, include.only="isDiagonal")
library(Matrix)
```

That is, we only throw a new warning in `library()` when (1) the package is already attached and (2) the current call uses `include.only=`.

Two extras:

1. If we read  `help(library)`, it becomes clear that `include.only=*` and `exclude=*` are  "twins"  and we should treat them consistently.

2. According to your proposal,

```
library(Matrix, include.only="isDiagonal")
library(Matrix, include.only="isDiagonal")
```

the 2nd call would give a warning, but of course, that's exactly the one case it should *not* give a warning.

----

Also, I think there are cases, where a warning is too much
(The caller of `library(<pkg>, include.only= *)` 
 only wanted to be to get *some* objects from <pkg> visible in search, but does not at all mind if there are more such objects)

and situations where the warning is appropropriate, because the caller wants carefully make *some* `<pkg>` objects visible in `search()`, but *not* others in order to get no / less conflicts later.

Hence, one could argue that we should  rather use `message()` than `warning()`...
__and__ maybe use a classed condition (in both cases).
